blocks.markdown: The **locative** case is used after **u** (in) and **na** (on/at) to describe a fixed location — never motion. Feminine **-a** becomes **-i**: *kuća* → **u kući** (in the house). This case only ever follows a preposition; it's never used on its own.

The same preposition **u** can also take the **accusative** instead, but with a completely different meaning: **u grad** (into the city — motion, accusative) vs. **u gradu** (in the city — location, locative). The case ending is what signals whether you're going somewhere or already there.

exercises.prompt: Živim u ___. (kuća → locative: kući — I live in the house.)
Radim u ___. (grad → locative — I work in the city.)
"u gradu" means location (in the city). What does "u grad" (accusative) signal instead?
